1001176.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse -ti (“ordinal-forming suffix”), occurring in inherited ordinal forms such as fimti (“fifth”), sétti (“sixth”), ellifti (“eleventh”) and tolfti (“twelfth”), ultimately reflecting a Proto-Germanic ordinal suffix *-tô.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk -te, Danish -te and Swedish -te (“ordinal-forming suffix”).

1001688.etyen:
Internationalism, borrowed from Latin Mimās, from Ancient Greek Μῐ́μᾱς (Mĭ́mās), the name of several figures in Greek mythology, including one of the Gigantes.
The moon was discovered by William Herschel in 1789 and was named after the mythological Mimas. The name was proposed by Herschel's son John Herschel in 1847, together with names for the other then-known moons of Saturn.
Compare the parallel adaptations Swedish Mimas, German Mimas, French Mimas, Polish Mimas, Spanish Mimas and English Mimas.

Whatever is received as a lease payment shall accrue to the Educational Endowment Fund

1005016.etyen:
Compound of bygsel (“land tenancy; lease payment; right of lease”) + sum (“sum, amount”), literally “lease sum”.
The second element sum (“sum, amount”) is from Middle Low German summe (“sum”) and German Summe (“sum”), ultimately from Latin summa (“total, sum”), the feminine of summus (“highest, greatest”), from Proto-Italic *supemos, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)úp-m̥mo-s (“uppermost, highest”).
